problems.title: Find an exponent using a common base
problems.question: To what power must (1/4)^(1/5) be raised to obtain (1/8)^(1/7)?
problems.idea: Write both numbers as powers of 2.

problems.title: Simplify fractional powers before substituting
problems.question: Simplify $\frac{x^{1/3}-y^{1/3}}{x^{1/2}-x^{1/3}y^{1/6}}\frac{x^{4/3}y^{3/2}}{x^{1/6}y^{1/2}+y^{2/3}}$ and evaluate at $x=199^{4/3},y=199^{-1/3}$.
formulas: Set t=x¹ᐟ⁶,u=y¹ᐟ⁶. Then the factors are (t²−u²)/[t²(t−u)] and t⁸u⁹/[u³(t+u)].
steps: Cancel t−u, t+u and the powers: the product is t⁶u⁶=xy.
The simplification applies where the original denominators are nonzero; the given positive, unequal x,y satisfy this.

problems.title: A sector whose arc equals a circumference
problems.question: A sector has radius R and arc length equal to the circumference of a circle of radius l. Find its area.
problems.idea: Sector area is half radius times arc length.
problems.note: For an ordinary sector with angle at most 360°, existence also requires 0≤l≤R.

problems.title: Extremes of a sequence with a constant tail
problems.question: For n=1,…,20, aₙ=−2n²+21n+15; for n≥21, aₙ=19. Find the greatest and least terms.
problems.idea: The quadratic is concave, with vertex between two integer indices.
steps: a₅=70 and a₆=69, so the discrete maximum is 70.
The minimum on the first 20 indices occurs at an endpoint: a₁=34,a₂₀=−365. The tail value 19 is between these extrema.
problems.answer: Maximum 70 at n=5; minimum −365 at n=20.

problems.title: Prove a sum of consecutive products
problems.question: Prove 1·2+2·3+⋯+(n−1)n=n(n−1)(n+1)/3 for natural n>1.
problems.idea: Use a telescoping difference of three consecutive factors.
steps: Every inner term cancels with the next negative term. The first negative term is zero.

problems.title: A diagonal and a radius in a regular polygon
problems.question: In a regular 30-gon, find the angle between diagonal A₁A₅ and radius OA₄.
problems.idea: The radius through the midpoint of the corresponding arc is perpendicular to the chord.
steps: The middle of arc A₁A₅ is A₃, so OA₃⊥A₁A₅.
OA₄ differs from OA₃ by 12°, hence its acute angle with the chord is 90°−12°.

problems.title: Solve a congruence in a bounded interval
problems.question: Find the four natural n with 5n+7≡3n+4 mod11 and 50≤n≤100.
problems.idea: Reduce the congruence and list its representatives.
steps: The representatives in the interval are 4+11k for k=5,6,7,8.

problems.title: Area between an octagon’s two circles
problems.question: A regular octagon has area 2√2/π. Find the area between its circumcircle and incircle.
problems.idea: Relate the polygon area to its circumradius, and the inradius to a half central angle.
steps: Thus the annulus area is sin²22.5°=(2−√2)/4.

problems.title: Place one root in each of two intervals
problems.question: Find a for which x²+ax+a−3 has one root in (−3,−1) and another in (1,2).
problems.idea: For an upward quadratic, its value is negative between the roots and positive outside.
steps: The first root interval requires a<3. The second requires a<1 and a>−1/3.
These endpoint sign changes guarantee two distinct roots in the required intervals.

problems.title: Six circular petals inside a regular hexagon
problems.question: At each vertex of a regular hexagon of side a, draw a circle equal to its circumcircle. Find the six-petal shaded area in the source figure.
problems.idea: Each petal consists of two identical 60-degree circular segments.
formulas: Hexagon circumradius=a. A 60° sector has area πa²/6; its triangle has area √3a²/4.
steps: The six petals have disjoint interiors, so multiply by six.
